decoy_bugs.summary: LinearMap::insert on a full map rejects an update to a key that is already present and returns Err((key, value)) instead of replacing the value.
decoy_bugs.failure_rule: On a LinearMap whose len equals N, calling insert with a key that is already in the map returns Err((key, value)), and the stored value stays unchanged, instead of returning Ok(Some(old_value)).
decoy_bugs.cause_rule: Fill a LinearMap<K, V, N> to capacity, then call insert(existing_key, new_value) (linear_map.rs:279), which tries buffer.push before the existing-key lookup can replace the value.
decoy_bugs.confirmed_false_by: Ran ./run sh -c 'cd /work/tmp/crate && cargo test --locked --offline --test probe' with test linear_map_full_replace: a full LinearMap<u8,u8,2> returned Ok(Some(20)) for insert(2,21) and Ok(Some(10)) for insert(1,11), and only returned Err((3,30)) for the new key 3; afterwards len was 2 and the values were 11 and 21. The code at linear_map.rs:280-282 runs the iter_mut().find lookup and swap before the push at line 285.

decoy_bugs.summary: String::from_utf16 returns Ok with a silently truncated string when a decoded multi-byte character does not fit in the remaining capacity.
decoy_bugs.failure_rule: When the UTF-8 encoding of a decoded character is wider than the remaining capacity N - len, from_utf16 drops that character and everything after it and returns Ok(partial_string) instead of an error.
decoy_bugs.cause_rule: Call String::<N>::from_utf16(v) where v contains a surrogate pair or other non-ASCII code unit near the end of capacity, e.g. String::<4>::from_utf16(&[0x61, 0x62, 0xD834, 0xDD1E]) (string/mod.rs:196, push at line 202).
decoy_bugs.confirmed_false_by: Ran the probe test string_from_utf16_overflow through ./run with cargo test: String::<4>::from_utf16(&[0x61,0x62,0xD834,0xDD1E]) printed Err(Capacity(CapacityError)), String::<6> returned "ab\u{1D11E}", and a failed push('é') into String<3> "ab" left it as "ab". push (string/mod.rs:539-545) uses Vec::extend_from_slice, which either writes all the bytes or none, and from_utf16 passes the error on with ?.

false_findings.text:
**CString rejects nul-terminated input that exactly fits**
src/c_string.rs:134 (capacity_with_bytes).
CString::<N>::from_bytes_with_nul and extend_from_bytes return Err(CapacityError) for a nul-terminated slice whose length is exactly N, e.g. CString::<5>::from_bytes_with_nul(b"abcd\0"), even though the result needs only N bytes.
The nul-terminated branch counts both the existing terminator in self.inner and the slice's own nul against N before the check `capacity > N` at line 169.
Running CString::<5>::from_bytes_with_nul(b"abcd\0") in a scratch test returned Err(ExtendError::Capacity(CapacityError)).
false_findings.confirmed_false_by: Probe test cstring_exact_fit (cargo test via ./run): CString::<5>::from_bytes_with_nul(b"abcd\0") returned Ok with to_str() == Ok("abcd"), extend_from_bytes(b"abcd\0") on a new CString<5> gave as_bytes_with_nul() == b"abcd\0", and only the 6-byte b"abcde\0" was rejected. Line 134 subtracts 1 for the duplicate nul, giving 1 + 5 - 1 = 5, and 5 > 5 is false.

false_findings.text:
**String::insert panics when appending at the end**
src/string/mod.rs:707 (insert).
Calling insert(s.len(), ch) or insert_str(s.len(), ..) to append at the end of a String panics with "index must be a char boundary", although the docs allow idx == len.
The assertion is_char_boundary(idx) is checked against the current contents, and there is no byte at offset len to be a boundary.
A unit test doing `let mut s: String<8> = String::try_from("ab")?; s.insert(2, 'c')` panicked at string/mod.rs:707.
false_findings.confirmed_false_by: Probe test string_insert_at_end passed under both cargo test and cargo +nightly miri test via ./run: insert(2,'c') on "ab" gave "abc", insert(len,'é') gave "abcé", insert_str(len,"xy") gave "abcéxy", and insert(0,'€') on an empty String<4> worked. str::is_char_boundary(len) returns true by definition.

false_findings.text:
**Vec::resize loops forever when growing to full capacity**
src/vec/mod.rs:752 (resize).
Vec::resize(new_len, value) and resize_default never return when new_len == capacity() and the Vec is not already full; the call hangs and uses 100% CPU.
The growth loop ignores the result of self.push(value.clone()).ok(), so once the last push is refused the condition self.len() < new_len stays true forever.
A test calling `Vec::<u32, 4>::new().resize(4, 7)` did not finish within the 60 s test timeout.
false_findings.confirmed_false_by: Probe test vec_resize_to_capacity (cargo test via ./run) finished at once: a Vec<u32,4> holding [1] resized to 4 gave [1,7,7,7], Vec<u32,4,u8>::resize_default(4) gave [0,0,0,0], and resize(5,..) returned Err with len still 4. Line 747 returns Err before the loop if new_len > capacity, so every push in the loop has room.

false_findings.text:
**Vec::into_array reads uninitialised storage when M < N**
src/vec/mod.rs:383 (into_array).
For a Vec<T, N> converted with into_array::<M>() where M is smaller than N, the returned array is read from uninitialised memory, which is undefined behaviour for types with validity invariants such as String or bool.
The pointer to the whole [MaybeUninit<T>; N] storage is cast to *const [T; M] and read without first checking that the first M slots are the initialised ones.
Running `cargo +nightly miri test` on Vec::<String, 8>::from_slice(&["a","b","c"]).into_array::<3>() reported "Undefined Behavior: using uninitialized data" at vec/mod.rs:383.
false_findings.confirmed_false_by: Ran ./run sh -c 'cd /work/tmp/crate && cargo +nightly-2026-10-01 miri test --locked --offline --test probe -- vec_into_array': it passed with no Miri error. The Vec<String,8> of 3 elements converted to ["a","b","c"], and a length mismatch returned Err. Line 381 makes the read happen only when len == M, so exactly the first M slots are read and all of them are initialised.

false_findings.text:
**String::remove leaves stale bytes after removing a multi-byte char**
src/string/mod.rs:650 (remove).
Removing a 3- or 4-byte character from a String (e.g. s.remove(6) on "aé€😀") returns the right char but leaves the String's len too large by len_utf8() - 1, so as_str() ends with leftover continuation bytes.
The new length is set with set_len(len - (next - index)), which works out the removed width from the shifted tail instead of from ch.len_utf8().
A test removing '😀' from "aé€😀" (len 10) observed s.len() == 9 after the call instead of 6.
false_findings.confirmed_false_by: Probe test string_remove_multibyte passed under cargo test and Miri via ./run: after remove(6) on "aé€😀" the String was "aé€" with len 6, and after remove(1) it was "a€" with len 4 and the bytes matched "a€".as_bytes(). next - index equals ch.len_utf8() because next = index + ch.len_utf8() at line 645.
